A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AGF research work, with readable text, figures, equations, and complete Appendices A–F. Corresponding material can be matched reliably across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical training experiments comparing AGF with gradient-based dynamics in Figures 3–6 and the diagonal-network example in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds a ReLU-network experiment on a CIFAR-10 subset in Figure 7. The original appendix experiment becomes Figure 8.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (3) change activation from reaching the accumulated-utility threshold to strictly exceeding it, refining boundary handling. The alternating utility-maximization and cost-minimization procedure otherwise remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 7 adds evaluation on a CIFAR-10 subset using two-layer ReLU networks. This substantially extends empirical coverage from the retained controlled regression and modular-addition settings to natural-image data.

E2.justification: The new CIFAR-10 comparison includes an optimal-linear-predictor reference line alongside AGF and gradient descent. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Figure 7 introduces a hidden-width sweep over 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 neurons, comparing AGF and gradient descent from the same extremely small initialization. These are added experimental settings; the retained experiments do not report substantive protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a sensitivity analysis testing how network width affects AGF–gradient-descent agreement and the transition from staircase to smooth loss curves. The appendix example of neurons returning to dormancy already appeared in v2 and is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiment does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 reports close jump tracking at small widths and weaker AGF agreement as wider networks develop smoother gradient-descent trajectories. Results in Figures 3–6 and the retained appendix diagonal-network illustration are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds distinct nonconjugate Fourier-magnitude assumptions and explicitly restricts the analysis to odd p; v2 treated odd p as a proof simplification and asserted extension to even p. Appendix F expands the trigonometric cancellation argument and restores a missing Fourier-magnitude cubed factor in the proof of Theorem F.6. The main results otherwise remain stable.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same four central contributions: AGF, diagonal-network convergence, unification of existing linear-network analyses, and Fourier-feature learning dynamics. The abstract's novelty claim remains, and neither version supplies a general AGF–gradient-flow convergence proof.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially sharpens applicability boundaries. It explains how overlapping activations and cost-minimization phases could produce smooth losses, discusses difficulties validating vanishing-initialization correspondence, and identifies population-level saddle transitions that AGF does not capture. These qualifications go beyond v2's general discussion of possible limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository link advertising code and experimental details in Appendix B and Figure 7, and makes the vector Gaussian initialization covariances explicit. The PDFs themselves do not provide the complete CIFAR-10 setup or establish the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Ben Arous et al., Kumar and Haupt, and Bantzis et al. Appendix A explicitly positions AGF as complementary to other theoretical regimes, while Appendix F newly acknowledges the similarity of Theorem F.3 and its proof to Morwani et al.'s existing maximum-margin analysis.

P1.justification: Section 6 is rewritten and Appendix B's explanation expanded, with smaller edits elsewhere; the overall organization and most prose remain intact. Venue, contact, and cross-reference text change, although some references incorrectly call Conjecture 4.1 a theorem.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 7, adjusts retained figure typography and time-axis labels from epochs to steps, and expands the appendix illustration's caption while renumbering it Figure 8. Existing plots and the document's general layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The added width experiment and more specific limitations make AGF's applicability easier to assess. Clearer assumptions, corrected appendix algebra, and code-access information also help. These gains are limited by incomplete experimental details within the PDF and inconsistencies, including theorem/conjecture cross-references and the retained p = 20 experiment alongside the newly explicit odd-p theory restriction.
